newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-PERU SHOCK URUGUAY IN COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU SHOCK URUGUAY IN COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Peru, fielding virtually an under-23 team, scored a shock 1-0 win over defending champions Uruguay in their Copa America group B game on Thursday.
Midfielder Martin Hidalgo hit the winner direct from a free kick to sink the 1995 winners, already under fire at home for their poor campaign in World Cup qualifiers.
The countries at the Copa America are fielding teams of varying strengths because the competition is being held in the middle of the continent's World Cup qualifying games.
Uruguay have not brought their top names but their squad contains a number of seasoned internationals, who were expected to overcome a Peru team that failed to qualify for last year's Olympic Games.
But Peru, after a shaky start, carved out the best chances and in the end deserved their win in a game played before a scant 5,000 crowd at 2,700 metres above sea level.
Peru, who had goalkeeper Miguel Miranda and striker Roberto Palacios as their only regular intervals in the team, finished with ten players after having Eddie Carazas sent off near the end.

Peru - Miguel Miranda, Jose Luis Reyna, Alfonso Dulanto, Miguel Rebosio, Martin Hidalgo, German Munoz, Erick Torres, Cesar Rosales (Frank Palomino), Eddie Carazas, Roberto Palacios (Waldir Saenz, 80), Paul Cominges (Alex Magallanes, 62)

Uruguay - Robert Siboldi, Tony Gomez, Hector Rodriguez, Eber Moas, Leonardo Ramos, Marcelo Saralegui, Nelson Abeijoon, Clever Romero (Gonzalo de los Santos, 46), Alvaro Recoba (Ruben Da Silva, 46), Sergio Martinez, Luis Romero.
